stem: A client receiving myelosuppressive chemotherapy presents with fever and neutropenia. Which plan should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Prompt evaluation and initiation of empiric antibacterial therapy without waiting for a confirmed infection source
options.B: Observation without treatment until fever has persisted for 24 hours
options.C: Delay antibacterial therapy until all culture results are final
options.D: Routine outpatient follow-up without urgent assessment because fever is expected with neutropenia

rationale: ASCO/IDSA guidance for adults with fever and neutropenia treated for malignancy endorses initial empiric antibacterial therapy within 1 hour of triage. Cultures and other evaluation are important, but treatment should not be delayed until a pathogen or source is definitively identified. Therefore A is the best plan; B, C, and D create inappropriate delay in a potentially serious complication.
educational_objective: Recognize fever with neutropenia during cancer therapy as requiring urgent evaluation and prompt empiric antibacterial treatment rather than waiting for definitive culture results.
source_organization: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) / American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO)
source_document_title: Outpatient Management of Fever and Neutropenia in Adults Treated for Malignancy: ASCO/IDSA Clinical Practice Guideline Update
source_version_date: Guideline update published 2018; current IDSA guideline page accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Recommendation: patients with febrile neutropenia should receive initial doses of empirical antibacterial therapy within 1 hour of triage and be monitored before outpatient discharge decisions
source_claim_supported: Adults with fever and neutropenia during malignancy treatment require prompt empiric antibacterial therapy; definitive culture confirmation should not delay initial treatment.

correction_summary: Converted the recognition-only source item into an urgent management item and anchored the timing directly to ASCO/IDSA guidance. Avoided inventing an ANC threshold in the stem and avoided requiring the nurse to independently prescribe antibiotics; the item asks what plan the nurse should anticipate.
audit_findings: A directly reflects guideline urgency. B, C, and D all create a treatment delay inconsistent with the recommendation. Because the stem states fever and neutropenia rather than asking the candidate to diagnose from an unsourced threshold, there is no unsupported numeric definition. One best answer and direct Physiological Adaptation relevance remain.
